[[File:MichaelHochberg.jpg|thumb|Michael Hochberg]]
'''Michael Hochberg''' (born 1980) is an American [[physicist]]. Hochberg's research includes [[silicon photonics]] and large-scale photonic integration. Much of his work in silicon photonics has been the product of collaborations with [[Tom Baehr-Jones|Thomas Baehr-Jones]].

==Degrees==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=May 2024}}
He obtained a BS in physics in 2002, an MS in applied physics in 2005 and a PhD in applied physics in 2006, all from the [[California Institute of Technology]]. Hochberg was a student of Professor [[Axel Scherer (professor)|Axel Scherer]].

==Awards and recognition==

In 2014, he was selected as a member of the [https://www.innovatorsunder35.com/ Technology Review TR 35 Asia]

He won a [https://www.nrf.gov.sg/funding-grants/nrf-fellowship Singapore NRF Fellowship in 2013].

In 2010, he was a National Academy of Sciences [https://www.nasonline.org/programs/scientific-meetings/frontiers-of-science/ Kavli Fellow].

He won a [[Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers|Presidential Early Career Award in Science and Engineering]] in 2009 through the U.S. Department of Defense.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the_press_office/PRESIDENT-HONORS-OUTSTANDING-EARLY-CAREER-SCIENTISTS/ |work=[[whitehouse.gov]] |title=President Honors Outstanding Early-Career Scientists |date=9 July 2009 |via=[[NARA|National Archives]] |access-date=2009-07-11 }}</ref>

Hochberg was awarded the [https://community.apan.org/wg/afosr/w/researchareas/12792/young-investigator-program-yip/ Air Force Office of Scientific Research Young Investigator] award in 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Air Force launches Young Investigators Research Program with $9.5 million investment|url=https://www.wpafb.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/401105/air-force-launches-young-investigators-research-program-with-95-million-investm/|access-date=2020-08-23|website=Wright-Patterson AFB|date=23 October 2007 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wpafb.af.mil/News/story/id/123072950/ |title=Air Force launches Young Investigators Research Program with $9.5 million investment |access-date=2008-12-08 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091221184729/http://www.wpafb.af.mil/news/story.asp?id=123072950 |archive-date=2009-12-21 }}</ref>

On graduation from his PHD program in 2006, he won the [https://www.demetriades.caltech.edu/ Demetriades-Tsafka Prize] for the best thesis in nanotechnology.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Demetriades - Tsafka - Kokkalis Prize|url=https://www.demetriades.caltech.edu/winners.html|access-date=2020-08-23|website=www.demetriades.caltech.edu}}</ref>

In 2002, he was awarded an [https://www.nsfgrfp.org/ National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship].<ref>{{Cite web|title=SNS iNews Thought Leader Michael Hochberg|url=http://old.stratnews.com/inews/profile/?clientid=2962/|access-date=2020-08-23|website=old.stratnews.com|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Companies founded==

Hochberg has been a founder at four companies. In each case his long-time collaborator [[Tom Baehr-Jones]] was one of the co-founders.

Simulant, which the first company to produce a distributed-memory implementation of finite difference time domain electromagnetic simulation tools.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Reading 12/6/2000|first=News Analysis Light|title=Startup Slashes Component Design Times|url=https://www.lightreading.com/ethernet-ip/startup-slashes-component-design-times/d/d-id/571929|access-date=2020-08-23|website=Light Reading|language=en}}</ref>  Simulant was acquired as part of the founding of Luxtera.

[[Luxtera]], which was founded later in his undergraduate career, pioneered building silicon integrated optics in a CMOS foundry. Acquired by [[Cisco]].

Silicon Lightwave Services. The first stand-alone integrated photonics design services company. Acquired by Marlin Investments.<ref>{{Cite web|title=StackPath|url=https://www.lightwaveonline.com/optical-tech/components/article/16654537/elenion-technologies-emerges-from-stealth-mode-with-silicon-photonics-optical-engines|access-date=2020-08-23|website=www.lightwaveonline.com|date=14 December 2016 }}</ref>

[[Elenion]] (formerly known as Coriant Advanced Technologies). A pioneer in building silicon photonic systems-on-chip, including coherent and data-center transceivers at speeds from 100G to 400G. Acquired by [[Nokia]].<ref>{{Cite web|last1=DeGrasse|first1=Martha|title=Nokia buys Elenion to target new markets with optical tech|url=https://www.lightreading.com/nokia-buys-elenion-to-target-new-markets-with-optical-tech/d/d-id/757596|access-date=2020-08-23|website=Light Reading|language=en}}</ref>

==Corporate Experience==

After Elenion was acquired by Nokia, Hochberg joined Nokia as CTO for Optical Subsystems from April 2020 to July 2021.

Hochberg left Nokia to join Luminous Computing serving as President of the startup then operating in Stealth mode.  After announcing its Series A funding in March 2022, the company publicly announced that Hochberg had already joined as president and would be running Engineering and Operations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Luminous Computing Announces Michael Hochberg as President |url=https://www.photonicsonline.com/doc/luminous-computing-announces-michael-hochberg-as-president-0001 |access-date=2022-03-16 |website=www.photonicsonline.com}}</ref>

==Academic positions==

He was an associate professor of electrical and computer engineering, materials science and chemical and biomolecular engineering at the [[University of Delaware]] in 2012-2014.

He held a professorship in electrical and computer engineering  [[National University of Singapore]] during 2012-2014.

He held a position as assistant professor in electrical engineering at the [[University of Washington]] from 2007 to 2012. and as an adjunct in physics for part of this period.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Orders|first=Karen|title=Electrical engineer's tiny technology has potential to revolutionize electronics|url=https://magazine.washington.edu/feature/electrical-engineers-tiny-technology-has-potential-to-revolutionize-electronics/|access-date=2020-08-23|website=UW Magazine — University of Washington Magazine}}</ref>

He was also the founding director of OpSIS: A US-based non-profit institute which pioneered the use of PDK’s and shared MPW runs for silicon photonics, with backing from the Air Force, Intel, Mentor Graphics, and several others.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2013-06-16|title=OpSIS Foundry {{!}} Optoelectronic Systems Integration in Silicon|url=http://opsisfoundry.org/|access-date=2020-08-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130616055847/http://opsisfoundry.org/|archive-date=2013-06-16}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Clark|first=Don|date=2011-02-01|title=Researchers Hope Sharing Costs Will Spur Optical Chips|url=https://blogs.wsj.com/digits/2011/02/01/researchers-hope-sharing-costs-will-spur-optical-chips/|access-date=2020-08-23|website=WSJ|language=en-US}}</ref> The OPSIS organization shut down in 2014 after its 5-year core funding expired.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Chrostowski |first1= Lucas |last2=Hochberg |first2=Michael |date=2015 |title= Silicon Photonics Design: From Devices to Systems |url=https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781316084168 |publisher= Cambridge University Press |page=22 |doi= 10.1017/CBO9781316084168 |isbn= 9781316084168}}</ref>

==Book==

He and Lukas Chrostowski co-authored a book called [https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/silicon-photonics-design/BF3CF13E8542BCE67FD2BBC7104ECEAB Silicon Photonics Design: From Devices to Systems] which has become a widely used text for courses in the field.

==Research interests and selected works==
The overall theme of Hochberg’s work has focused on scaling complexity and integrating new functionality into silicon photonic platforms.  He has contributed to a number of areas within the broader field of silicon photonics, including:
* Platform integration, fabless infrastructure and PDK Development
** [https://www.degruyter.com/view/journals/nanoph/3/4-5/article-p205.xml An overview of some of his team's early work on PDK's]
** [https://www.nature.com/articles/nphoton.2010.172 Towards Fabless Silicon Photonics]  An article predicting growth to a multibillion-dollar industry by 2020, published in 2010, and showing exponential growth in the complexity of silicon photonic circuits over time
** [https://www.nature.com/articles/nphoton.2012.66/ Myths and Rumours of Silicon Photonics] An article debunking a number of popular misconceptions about the field.
** [https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/stamp/stamp.jsp?tp=&arnumber=6449374 Silicon Photonics:  The next fabless semiconductor industry] A review of the current state of fabless silicon photonics in 2013.
* [https://www.osapublishing.org/oe/abstract.cfm?uri=OE-13-14-5216 Hybrid integration of organic materials with silicon waveguides], including the first demonstrations that slot waveguides could be integrated with electrooptic polymers to produce [https://aip.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.2909656 exceptionally low drive voltage modulators] 
* [https://www.nature.com/articles/nphoton.2017.95 Quantum Optics in Silicon]
* [https://www.nature.com/articles/nphoton.2017.93 Artificial intelligence and deep learning]
** This work resulted in the creation of two startup companies, [https://lightmatter.co/ Lightmatter] and [[Lightelligence]], both spinoffs of [[Dirk Englund]]’s [https://www.rle.mit.edu/qp/ group at MIT]
* [https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/5437305/authors#authors Label-free Biosensor Arrays] in silicon began as a collaboration with [https://www.genalyte.com/ Genalyte]
* [https://www.osapublishing.org/oe/abstract.cfm?uri=oe-26-7-7920 Lasers] and laser integration in silicon
* [https://www.nature.com/articles/nmat1719 Nonlinear optics in silicon]
* [https://www.osapublishing.org/oe/abstract.cfm?uri=oe-18-12-12127 Mid-infrared waveguides] and resonators in silicon
* [https://aip.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.1871360 High-Q ring resonators] in silicon
* [https://www.osapublishing.org/oe/abstract.cfm?uri=oe-21-1-1310 Inverse design and computationally automated optimization]
* Active and high-speed photonic-electronic devices, including [https://www.osapublishing.org/oe/abstract.cfm?uri=oe-20-11-12014 modulators] and [https://www.osapublishing.org/oe/abstract.cfm?uri=oe-21-23-28387 photodetectors]
* [https://www.osapublishing.org/abstract.cfm?uri=ofc-2018-Th4D.4 Photonic-electronic integration and transceivers]
* [https://www.nature.com/articles/micronano201671/fig_tab Optical Switching]
* [https://www.nature.com/articles/nature07545 Optical actuation and force sensing]
